exposure: Time since birth (baseline, 1 month, 4 months, 6 months)
cohort: Consecutive sample of 586 mothers recruited within 48 hours of birth in maternity wards in all public hospitals and 29 of 35 private maternity clinics nationwide in Cyprus
finding: While breastfeeding initiation was high, breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding rates in Cyprus declined significantly by 6 months, with mode of delivery, maternal education, and family income identified as key determinants.
mod_finding: Mothers who gave birth vaginally were three to four times more likely to initiate both breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding.
